svg.text: Measurement record. Fill this before you believe the report.
Points sit on the opening, not in the aisle. A screen glance is not a point. A nameplate is not a load.

g.text: A. Cooling unit — one block per unit that serves this room
Unit: ____________ Opening: supply / return Date of reading: ____________
Supply opening. At least two points. Average = (T1 + T2) / 2
T1 ________ T2 ________ Average ________ Points were on the opening: Y / N
Return opening. Three points. Average = (T1 + T2 + T3) / 3
If you have only one return point, do not call it the return. Go back and take three.
B. Cabinets the report will name. A row you did not walk is not in this table.
Cabinet (id stays in the project file): ____________
Front inlet ________ Rear outlet ________ Same point exists in the model: Y / N
Do not enter one room-average temperature and pretend it is every inlet.
C. Heat. Read the feed, not the nameplate.
Source: cabinet strip / upstream unit that feeds it: ____________ Reading: ________
If the model still uses the nameplate, the picture is of a different load. Replace it and rerun.
D. Dates. A mixed year is not a calibration.
Measurement date: ____________ Layout date in the report: ____________
If they differ, these temperatures belong to: the measurement layout / the report layout
E. Correction. Name the input, or write not corrected.
Changed: missing blank / blocked grille / open aisle / unit off / nameplate / brochure setpoint / none
Rerun of the same scene after that change: Y / N
If you cannot name a further input, stop. Write: not corrected. Do not blend the plot toward the meter.
